newsitem.title: EGYPT: Dutch minister sees larger EU role in peace process.
newsitem.headline: Dutch minister sees larger EU role in peace process.

text.p: Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo said on Tuesday the European Union hoped in the next month to contribute to the resumption of peace talks between Syria and Israel.
Van Mierlo, who visited Cairo as the EU council of ministers chairman, spoke after talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa.

He also criticised Israeli settlement of occupied Arab land: "We have also said from the European side that we think the settlement policy is negative to the peace process so we are criticising this, as the Americans do also."

Mierlo noted the EU now has special representative for the Middle East, Miguel Angel Moratinos, who is due to visit Egypt on Thursday: "I think that increasingly the role of Europe also will be important in the next coming months."

The Netherlands holds the rotating presidency of the 15-nation EU for the first half of this year. Last year the bloc appointed Moratinos to boost Europe's role in the U.S.-dominated peace negotiations in the region.

Asked if he had proposals for bringing Syria and Israel together, van Mierlo said: "Not specific proposals, but we are trying to do the utmost to get Syria again in the peace process. Our man Moratinos was already prepared to visit, also on the request of the Israeli prime minister, to (Syrian) President (Hafez) Assad.
"I think in the coming month it is not impossible that Europe can play a positive role to get Syria in the peace process again," van Mierlo said.
Israeli-Syrian talks were suspended by Israel before its national election last May.

Syria wants talks resumed from the point where they left off with the previous Israeli government but Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he will not guarantee to accept anything agreed in earlier talks. Syria wants the full return of the occupied Golan Heights, a position rejected by Netanyahu.
Mierlo said Israel and the United States have warmed to an EU role in the peace process, and Europe and Washington should work together.
"We should avoid that the Americans played a role to the benefit of the Israelis and Europe only back the Palestinians," van Mierlo said.
